$comment: Cisco portfolio coverage map. Sourcetypes come from Splunk's 'Integrated Enterprise Value for Cisco data' table and the Cisco Security Cloud App user guide; capability lists come from vendor feature and telemetry documentation. A capability is observable only when a documented event stream shows it. cimModels lists a model only when the vendor or add-on documents the mapping; cimNote explains every empty list. Edit this file, then run `python -m splunk_uc generate-cisco-coverage` and `audit-cisco-coverage --check`.

collection.note: Duo Admin API integration key, secret key, and API hostname (api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com) created under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. The authentication_v2 result values are lowercase; v1 values are uppercase.

capabilities.name: MFA authentication outcomes
capabilities.telemetry: Authentication log: one event per sign-in with result, reason, factor, user, application, access device IP and location.
capabilities.cimNote: Cisco Security Cloud lists CIM mappings as beta and publishes no per-sourcetype model; Splunk Security Content detections search the raw Duo fields.
capabilities.outcome: Shows who failed or was denied the second factor, push fatigue, and fraud reports, so account takeover is caught at the sign-in step.

capabilities.name: Administrator and policy changes
capabilities.telemetry: Administrator log: action, actionlabel, object, username, description for policy, user, bypass-code, and integration changes.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Change mapping for the Duo administrator log.
capabilities.outcome: Catches policies that bypass or weaken MFA and bypass codes issued outside change control, before an attacker uses them.

capabilities.name: Unified activity log
capabilities.telemetry: Activity log v2: action.name, actor.name, actor.type, outcome.result, access_device.ip.address, access_device.location.country, target.name.
capabilities.cimNote: Nested Duo fields; no documented CIM mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Gives one stream of admin and user actions with actor location, so unusual admin sign-ins are visible across the whole Duo tenant.

capabilities.name: Trust Monitor security events
capabilities.telemetry: Trust Monitor events surfaced through the Admin API: Duo's own risk detections on authentications and devices.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Alerts mapping for Trust Monitor events.
capabilities.outcome: Brings Duo's own risk findings into the SOC queue so they are triaged with the rest of the alerts instead of only inside the Duo console.

capabilities.name: Telephony credit usage
capabilities.telemetry: Telephony log: SMS and phone-call factor deliveries and the credits they consume.
capabilities.cimNote: Telephony credit use is a billing signal; no CIM model applies.
capabilities.outcome: Warns before telephony credits run out, which would stop SMS and phone-call MFA, and exposes toll-fraud style bursts.

capabilities.name: Endpoint inventory and posture
capabilities.telemetry: Endpoint objects from the Admin API: operating system and browser versions, and device health attributes for devices that authenticate.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Inventory mapping for Duo endpoints.
capabilities.outcome: Shows which out-of-date operating systems and browsers still reach protected apps, so device-health policy can be tightened with evidence.

capabilities.name: User and account state
capabilities.telemetry: User and account objects from the Admin API: enrollment, status (active, bypass, disabled, locked out), and attached phones and tokens.
capabilities.cimNote: Object snapshots, not events; no CIM model applies.
capabilities.outcome: Finds users left in bypass status or never enrolled, which are the accounts where MFA silently does not apply.

capabilities.name: DNS-layer security
capabilities.telemetry: DNS log: action, domain/query, category, blocked_category, identities, identity_type, reply_code, src_ip, user.
capabilities.cimNote: Splunk Security Content sample events from the 7569 add-on carry tag, eventtype, and the Network_Resolution fields query, query_type, record_type, reply_code, and src. Umbrella's allow/block action is not a Network_Resolution field, so block analysis stays on the raw sourcetype.
capabilities.outcome: Shows blocked malware, phishing, and command-and-control lookups per identity, so infected devices are found from the first DNS request.

capabilities.name: Secure web gateway
capabilities.telemetry: Proxy log: action, dest, http_method, http_user_agent, category, amp_disposition, amp_malwarename, sha256, dlp_status, isolateAction.
capabilities.cimNote: Splunk Security Content sample events from the 7569 add-on carry tag, eventtype, and the Web fields action, dest, http_method, http_user_agent, status, url, and bytes_in/bytes_out.
capabilities.outcome: Shows malicious downloads and risky web categories per user, so web-borne threats are contained before they spread.

capabilities.name: Cloud-delivered firewall
capabilities.telemetry: Firewall log: action, dest_ip, dest_port, identity, rule_id, bytes_in, bytes_out, datacenter, tunnel_id.
capabilities.cimNote: Field names follow CIM (action, dest_ip, dest_port, bytes_in, bytes_out), but the Security Content sample shows no tag field, so Network_Traffic acceleration is not confirmed.
capabilities.outcome: Shows which tunnels and identities hit block rules, so policy gaps and blocked exfiltration attempts are visible per site.

capabilities.name: Cloud IPS
capabilities.telemetry: Intrusion events from the Secure Access IPS: signature, classification, severity, source and destination.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented Intrusion_Detection tag for the Secure Access intrusion feed.
capabilities.outcome: Shows exploit attempts the cloud IPS saw, so remote users and branches get the same intrusion visibility as the data center.

capabilities.name: Data loss prevention
capabilities.telemetry: DLP events: rule matched, destination application, file, identity, and action.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM DLP mapping for the Secure Access DLP feed.
capabilities.outcome: Shows sensitive data leaving through web and SaaS uploads per user, so data-protection incidents are handled with evidence.

capabilities.name: Zero trust network access
capabilities.telemetry: ZTNA access, flow, and enrollment logs for private application access.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM mapping for ZTNA logs.
capabilities.outcome: Shows who reached which private application and which attempts were denied, which is the audit trail zero-trust access promises.

capabilities.name: Remote access VPN
capabilities.telemetry: RAVPN session logs from Secure Access.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM mapping for the RAVPN feed.
capabilities.outcome: Shows VPN connections by user, country, and posture result, so impossible travel and failed-posture logins are caught.

capabilities.name: Cloud application discovery
capabilities.telemetry: App discovery records: SaaS applications seen, risk, and usage.
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM model applies to SaaS discovery inventory.
capabilities.outcome: Shows unsanctioned SaaS applications in use, so shadow IT is reviewed before it holds company data.

capabilities.name: Admin audit trail
capabilities.telemetry: Admin audit log: dashboard changes to policies, identities, and settings.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Change mapping for the audit feed.
capabilities.outcome: Shows who changed security policy and when, so an unsafe allow-list entry can be traced to an owner and a ticket.

capabilities.name: Malware detection
capabilities.telemetry: Events with event_type_id 1090519054 (Threat Detected) and 1090519084 (DFC Threat Detected).
capabilities.cimNote: The 3686 CIM add-on maps the legacy AMP input, not cisco:se.
capabilities.outcome: Shows which hosts had malware or a malicious network connection detected, so incident response starts from the right machine.

capabilities.name: Quarantine success and failure
capabilities.telemetry: Events with event_type_id 553648143 (Threat Quarantined) and 2164260880 (Quarantine Failure).
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM mapping for cisco:se.
capabilities.outcome: Shows detections the agent could not quarantine, which are the infections still live on a host and need a human.

capabilities.name: Retrospective detection
capabilities.telemetry: Events with event_type_id 553648147 (Retrospective Detection): a file seen earlier is now known malicious.
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM mapping for cisco:se.
capabilities.outcome: Finds every host that ran a file before it was known to be bad, so a late verdict still leads to cleanup.

capabilities.name: Exploit prevention
capabilities.telemetry: Events with event_type_id 1090519103 (Exploit Prevention).
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM mapping for cisco:se.
capabilities.outcome: Shows memory-exploit attempts the agent blocked, which point to targeted attacks against unpatched applications.

capabilities.name: Incident import
capabilities.telemetry: XDR incidents and incident summaries imported on the configured schedule.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Alerts mapping for XDR incidents.
capabilities.outcome: Puts XDR's correlated incidents next to the rest of the security data, so analysts see age and status of every open incident in one place.

capabilities.name: Promotion to Enterprise Security findings
capabilities.telemetry: Incident summaries written as notable-ready events when promotion is enabled.
capabilities.cimNote: Consumed by Enterprise Security, not a CIM data model.
capabilities.outcome: Confirms that XDR incidents actually arrive as Enterprise Security findings, so the SOC queue is not silently missing them.

capabilities.name: Behavioral alarms
capabilities.telemetry: SNA alarms pulled from the Manager API, with severity Critical, Major, Minor, Trivial, or Info.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM mapping for SNA alarms.
capabilities.outcome: Shows hosts behaving like scanners, data hoarders, or beaconing bots from network flow analysis, including devices that run no agent.

capabilities.name: Host risk scoring
capabilities.telemetry: SNA risk records per host.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Ranks internal hosts by accumulated network risk, so investigation time goes to the riskiest devices first.

capabilities.name: Alarm promotion to notables
capabilities.telemetry: Alarms written as notable-ready events at the selected severities.
capabilities.cimNote: Consumed by Enterprise Security, not a CIM data model.
capabilities.outcome: Confirms that the SNA alarms the SOC agreed to handle reach the Enterprise Security queue.

capabilities.name: Enterprise flow records
capabilities.outcome: Gives raw east-west traffic records for investigations that need the conversation, not just the alarm.
capabilities.notObservableReason: Cisco Security Cloud documents SNA alarms as sourcetype cisco:sna. It does not document a Flow Collector sourcetype. Traffic queries are an SMC API with no published Splunk field list.

capabilities.name: Layer 4 firewall
capabilities.telemetry: L4 firewall and session summary logs from MCD gateways.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented Network_Traffic tag for MCD logs.
capabilities.outcome: Shows denied and allowed cloud traffic per gateway, so exposed cloud workloads and blocked lateral movement are visible.

capabilities.name: URL and FQDN egress filtering
capabilities.telemetry: URL filter, FQDN filter, FQDN resolution, and SNI logs.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented Web mapping for MCD filter logs.
capabilities.outcome: Shows cloud workloads trying to reach blocked destinations, which is how compromised instances call home.

capabilities.name: Antivirus, IPS, and malicious source blocking
capabilities.telemetry: Antivirus, DPI (intrusion), and malicious-source logs.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented Intrusion_Detection or Malware tag for MCD logs.
capabilities.outcome: Shows exploit attempts, malware transfers, and known-bad sources stopped at the cloud edge, per application.

capabilities.name: WAF and layer 7 DoS protection
capabilities.telemetry: WAF and L7 DoS logs.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Shows attacks against public cloud applications and whether the WAF blocked them.

capabilities.name: Data loss prevention
capabilities.telemetry: DLP logs from MCD gateways.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM DLP mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Shows sensitive data patterns leaving cloud workloads, so cloud data exposure is caught at the network layer.

capabilities.name: TLS decryption health
capabilities.telemetry: TLS log and TLS error records.
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM model covers decryption errors.
capabilities.outcome: Shows where TLS inspection fails, which is traffic the other controls cannot see into.

capabilities.name: Audit and system logs
capabilities.telemetry: MCD audit logs and gateway system logs.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Change mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Shows who changed cloud security policy and gateway health events, so outages and risky changes have an owner.

capabilities.name: Message threat verdicts
capabilities.telemetry: Message log type: messages ETD analysed, with verdicts for phishing, malicious, spam, and business email compromise.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented CIM Email mapping for cisco:etd.
capabilities.outcome: Shows which mailboxes receive phishing and business email compromise, so targeted users are warned and messages pulled.

capabilities.name: Audit log
capabilities.outcome: Shows who remediated or released messages, so manual overrides of email security are accountable.
capabilities.notObservableReason: The add-on writes Connection, Audit, and Message logs to the single sourcetype cisco:etd and publishes no field that tells them apart. Message logs are covered by restricting the input to Message Logs.

capabilities.name: Container process execution
capabilities.telemetry: process_exec events: process_exec.process.binary, arguments, pod_name, pod_namespace, cluster_name, node_name.
capabilities.cimNote: Nested Tetragon fields; Security Content searches them raw rather than through the Endpoint model.
capabilities.outcome: Shows shells, package managers, and recon tools started inside running containers, which should never happen in production pods.

capabilities.name: Process network connections
capabilities.telemetry: process_connect events: process_connect.destination_ip, destination_port, process binary, pod and namespace.
capabilities.cimNote: No documented Network_Traffic mapping.
capabilities.outcome: Ties each outbound connection to the exact container process, so a pod calling an unknown address is traced in one step.

capabilities.name: Kernel probe policy hits
capabilities.telemetry: process_kprobe events: process_kprobe.function_name, process_kprobe.policy_name, process binary, pod.
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM model covers kernel function tracing.
capabilities.outcome: Shows hits on TracingPolicies for sensitive kernel calls, such as privilege changes and module loads, inside the cluster.

capabilities.name: Per-flow permit and deny decisions
capabilities.outcome: Confirms that switch-embedded enforcement is sending its decisions, and gives the deny trail for segmentation audits.
capabilities.notObservableReason: Cisco documents syslog export of permit and deny records and publishes no Splunk sourcetype or field list.

capabilities.name: IPFIX flow telemetry
capabilities.outcome: Gives traffic trends through segmented zones, which is needed before tightening a policy from monitor to enforce.
capabilities.notObservableReason: Cisco documents IPFIX export from enforcement points and publishes no Splunk sourcetype or field list.

capabilities.name: Timescape management history
capabilities.notObservableReason: Cisco documents Timescape event history as reviewed in the Timescape UI and not exported; CSV export covers only the current page.
capabilities.outcome: Would show who changed or deployed Hypershield policy; today this audit trail stays in the Hypershield console.

capabilities.name: Fabric assertion notifications
capabilities.telemetry: Splunk webhook notifications for latched assertions: timestamp, criticality, breadcrumb link to the fabric blueprint. Assertion conditions are True, False, Warning, or Unknown.
capabilities.cimNote: Fabric health checks have no CIM model.
capabilities.outcome: Pages the network team when a fabric health check fails at the device, port, or fabric level, before users notice.

capabilities.name: Configuration change commits
capabilities.outcome: Lines up fabric failures with the configuration commit just before them, which shortens root cause for change-induced outages.
capabilities.notObservableReason: Commit summaries are included in the same Splunk webhook notification as assertion changes, and Cisco publishes no JSON field that separates them.

capabilities.name: Fabric, node, and device inventory
capabilities.outcome: Keeps an independent record of which switches are bound to which fabric nodes, for audits and capacity planning.
capabilities.notObservableReason: The fabrics, nodes, and devices API is not collected by a Splunk add-on, and Cisco publishes no sourcetype or field extraction for it.

capabilities.name: HSR ring faults
capabilities.telemetry: %HSR_ALARM-3-HSR_PARTIALFAULT (one ring port down) and %HSR_ALARM-2-HSR_RINGFAULT (both ring ports down), each with a '- event cleared' variant.
capabilities.cimNote: Ring state is an operational fault; no CIM model applies.
capabilities.outcome: Warns when a seamless-redundancy ring has lost its spare path, so it is repaired before a second failure stops the process network.

capabilities.name: PTP clock changes
capabilities.telemetry: %PTP-6-PARENT_CLOCK_CHANGE, %PTP-6-GRANDMASTER_CLOCK_CHANGE, and %PTP-6-GRANDMASTER_CLOCK_CHANGE_TO_LOCAL system messages.
capabilities.cimNote: Clock topology changes have no CIM model.
capabilities.outcome: Shows grandmaster and parent clock changes that break timing for motion control and protection relays.

capabilities.name: PRP VLAN tagging faults
capabilities.telemetry: %PRP_MSG-4-PRP_VLANTAG system messages.
capabilities.cimNote: No CIM model applies.
capabilities.outcome: Flags PRP configuration faults that silently remove the duplicate-path protection a parallel redundancy network is built for.

capabilities.name: Hardware alarm relay state
capabilities.notObservableReason: Relay contact state is shown by 'show facility-alarm status' and SNMP; only alarms configured with 'alarm facility <type> syslog' reach syslog, and those are covered by the HSR and PTP capabilities.
capabilities.outcome: Would confirm the physical alarm relay wired to the plant control system tripped; check it through SNMP or the CLI.
